## Performance AFTER receipt

Merge: `2d5b1a9c19c0c771a43a4ef46f87a54398e2608c`. After the reinstall/bounce, daemon PID **19370** was verified in both ping responses and by the listening socket at both window edges. This closes the post-deployment measurement owed by the performance verdicts.

| Measurement | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| UTC window, November 18, 2026 | 03:15:32.321241 to 03:15:52.506222 | 03:51:25.050131 to 03:51:45.257404 |
| Same daemon PID within window | 46800 | 19370 |
| Monotonic counter interval | 20.184645 s | 20.207214 s |
| `spawns.total` | 793 -> 793 | 447 -> 456 |
| Exact counted daemon launches | 0; **0.0000/s** | 9; **0.4454/s** |
| Machine launches/s, 20.0 s probe | **111.9/s** | **232.1/s** |
| Parent cumulative CPU time | 11:23.49 -> 11:26.38; +2.89 CPU s | 0:34.56 -> 0:38.21; +3.65 CPU s |
| Parent CPU during sample | approximately 14.3% of one core; baseline ps snapshots bracket the counter window | **18.05% of one core** over the separately timed 20.222464 s ps interval |
| RSS, KiB | 142768 -> 142256 | 228144 -> 137008 |
| RSS, MiB | 139.42 -> 138.92 | 222.80 -> 133.80 |
| Daemon uptime at ps snapshots | 50:35 -> 50:55 | 01:17 -> 01:37 |

Commands: `pij-rs --json ping` twice, selecting `data.pid` and `data.spawns` in Python; `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json`; exact-pid `/bin/ps -p <pid> -o pid=,ppid=,%cpu=,rss=,time=,etime=,comm=`. UTC timestamps and monotonic elapsed times were captured with the responses. No build, test, install or bounce was performed by this measurement.

### AFTER daemon counters, every reported operation

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ddocs.community` | 12 | 14 | +2 |
| `gh.delivered` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `git.community` | 28 | 35 | +7 |
| `git.pa-watchdog-common-dir` | 22 | 22 | 0 |
| `ps.registration-native-process` | 133 | 133 | 0 |
| `ps.sidecar-process-group` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tmux.control-client` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tmux.new-window` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `tmux.pipe-pane attach` | 121 | 121 | 0 |
| `tmux.rename-window` | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| `tmux.set-options tap owner` | 121 | 121 | 0 |

The site deltas sum to the total delta, **9**: `git.community` 0.3464/s and `ddocs.community` 0.0990/s. All counted launches in this window were community writers; the process-probe and tmux counters did not move. In the BEFORE window, all 20 reported operation counters were unchanged.

### Interpretation and limits

The observed machine-wide increase is **120.2 launches/s**, and parent CPU was higher in this sample. These are not controlled estimates of #240's incremental cost: the daemon was only 77-97 seconds old after reconnecting, versus roughly 51 minutes before, and the shared machine's workload differed. The RSS fall within the fresh-daemon window is an observation, not proof of a fixed leak or lower steady-state memory.

Do not subtract the absolute counters across the bounce. Compare each window's same-PID deltas. The daemon counter is exact for its instrumented launch sites, but does not count the Copilot-owned statusline CLI's launches or in-process CPU. Source review established that the new ownership probe itself launches nothing; these counters alone do not prove that.

Machine per-parent/command attribution is a lower bound. In particular `statusline_runs_seen_per_s` searches for the managed script's argv marker, which can disappear when the script execs `pij-rs statusline copilot`; **0.1/s is not the true render rate**. The scheduled rate remains one render per 10 s per rendering session, plus event-driven renders. The busy-polling sampler also contributes overhead in both measurements.

**Owed AFTER measurement: completed.** The non-blocking C34 follow-up about the self-plus-64-ancestors bound (65 reader calls) is unchanged; this receipt does not claim a per-render latency benchmark or a universal no-regression result.
